Selkirk Copper Announces US$30 Million Convertible Debenture Financing
7 min read
SCMI QRC
British Columbia and Pelly Crossing, Yukon--(Newsfile Corp. - November 23, 2026) - Selkirk Copper Mines Inc. SCMI (FSE: IO20) (OTCQX: SKRKF) ("Selkirk Copper" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has entered into a binding term sheet (the "Term Sheet") with Queen's Road Capital Investment Ltd. ("Queen's Road") for a private placement (the "Offering") of US$30 million (approximately CAD$42.9 million) principal amount of unsecured convertible debentures (the "Debentures") of the Company.
Proceeds from the Offering will be used to fund the exploration, development, and restart of the Company's Minto Project located in central Yukon and for general corporate purposes.
M. Colin Joudrie, President & CEO of the Company, commented: "Queen's Road is a seasoned investor and financing partner to the mining industry with a track record of recognizing and investing in high-quality exploration and development companies through the cycle. The investment by Queen's Road is another step in our planned approach to the restart of mining and mineral processing activities that will deliver high-quality copper-gold-silver concentrates in a timely manner into a global market that is short of concentrate. Further, the investment by Queen's Road is a vote of confidence in our plan and recognition of the good work completed by our team over the last 18 months."
Warren Gilman, Chairman and CEO of Queen's Road, commented: "Queen's Road is delighted to work with Selkirk Copper and the Selkirk First Nation to see the restart of the Minto Mine become a reality. Minto represents a classic Queen's Road investment, a tested copper producer in a supportive jurisdiction with experienced and aligned partners. I have known and worked with Colin Joudrie for many years and look forward to supporting his Selkirk Copper team."
The Debentures will be governed by a debenture certificate to be issued by the Company in favor of Queen's Road and which will set out the terms contained in the Term Sheet. The Debentures will be convertible at the option of the holder, in part or in whole, into common shares of the Company at a price per share of CAD$1.00, based on the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate and subject to adjustment under certain events (the "Conversion Price"). The Conversion Price represents a 37% premium to the daily volume-weighted average trading price ("VWAP") of the Company's shares on the TSXV on November 20, 2026, being the last trading day before execution of the Term Sheet. The Company will be entitled to redeem the Debentures at par within a period of fourteen days following the third anniversary of the date of the issuance of the Debentures. Should the Company exercise its right to redeem the Debentures during this period, the holders are entitled to convert all of the outstanding Debentures into Common Shares at a price per share of C$0.92, equal to a 20% premium to the 3-day volume-weighted average trading price ("VWAP") at the date of this announcement.

VeloSano Raises $20.2 Million for Cancer Research
The 2026 total is the latest milestone for the Cleveland Clinic fundraising initiative that has supported cancer research since 2014.
Updated on Nov. 22, 2026 in Philanthropy
VeloSano raised $20.2 million in 2026 for cancer research at Cleveland Clinic and Cleveland Clinic Children's, bringing its total to more than $115 million since 2014. AI Illustration. Upload story photo >
Live Poll
Do you think community fundraising events meaningfully help advance cancer research?
▲ Yes ▼ No
VeloSano raised $20.2 million in 2026 to support cancer research at Cleveland Clinic and Cleveland Clinic Children's. The initiative has raised more than $115 million for cancer research since 2014.
Why it matters
The funds support local cancer research, including projects selected through a competitive grant process that benefits the Cleveland community. Sustained philanthropic support helps the region's health system pursue research that might otherwise lack funding.
VeloSano's 2026 total of $20.2 million came from more than 30,000 donors making direct or legacy gifts, with more than 5,000 participants and volunteers supporting its signature events. The source does not specify the breakdown between event proceeds and direct donations.
The players
Cleveland Clinic
A nonprofit academic medical center based in Cleveland, Ohio, known for its cancer treatment and research programs and as the recipient of VeloSano funds.
Cleveland Clinic Children's
The pediatric arm of Cleveland Clinic, which receives VeloSano funding for pediatric cancer research.
Cleveland Metroparks Zoo
A major zoo in Cleveland, Ohio, that hosted the June 2026 Trike and Bike children's ride for pediatric cancer research.
The details
VeloSano funds are partly awarded through a competitive application process called VeloSano Pilot Grants. In September 2026, nearly 2,650 riders and 800 volunteers took part in the Bike to Cure weekend, and in June 2026 children ages 3 to 10 rode at Cleveland Metroparks Zoo in the Trike and Bike event for pediatric cancer research.
Timeline
2014 — VeloSano initiative launched, beginning its cumulative fundraising.
June 2026 — Trike and Bike children's ride held at Cleveland Metroparks Zoo.
September 2026 — Bike to Cure weekend held with nearly 2,650 riders.
March 9, 2027 — Registration opens for 2027 VeloSano events.
September 10–11, 2027 — VeloSano Bike to Cure Weekend scheduled.
Philanthropy Trajectory
The $20.2 million raised in 2026 extends VeloSano's cumulative trajectory of more than $115 million since its 2014 launch at Cleveland Clinic. Its more than 300 funded projects and $107 million in extramural grants show how a community fundraising base can leverage additional outside research money.
Residents who want to participate can register for 2027 VeloSano events beginning March 9. Donations and event participation directly support cancer research at Cleveland Clinic and Cleveland Clinic Children's.
The takeaway
Cancer research funding in Cleveland depends heavily on recurring community giving, and participation in events like Bike to Cure is one concrete way residents can contribute. Supporting local fundraisers helps sustain research pipelines beyond any single year's total.
What happens next
Registration for the 2027 VeloSano events opens March 9, 2027, ahead of the Bike to Cure Weekend scheduled for September 10–11, 2027.

articles.snippet:
Huntington Ingalls received two Navy modifications totaling approximately $20 million for submarine-valve engineering and cruiser planning-yard support.
The post Huntington Ingalls Receives $20 Million Across Submarine And Cruiser Support Awards appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Huntington Ingalls Receives $20 Million Across Submarine And Cruiser Support Awards
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 9:06 PM
Huntington Ingalls Receives $20 Million Across Submarine And Cruiser Support Awards
Huntington Ingalls received two Navy modifications totaling approximately $20 million for submarine-valve engineering and cruiser planning-yard support.
The company’s Newport News business received a $10.1 million modification for engineering and design work involving standard Navy valves installed on nuclear-powered submarines.
Two Naval Engineering Programs
Work on the submarine-valve effort will be performed in Newport News, Virginia. The Navy obligated $1.5 million in fiscal 2027 operations-and-maintenance funding at award, with that initial amount scheduled to expire at the end of the fiscal year.
Huntington Ingalls’ Ingalls Shipbuilding division received a separate $9.8 million modification exercising the seventh option year for CG-47-class integrated planning-yard services.
The work includes design, planning, and material support for cruiser maintenance and modernization. It will be performed in Pascagoula, Mississippi, through December 2027.
No funding was obligated when the option was exercised. The Navy expects to commit funds as specific requirements arise.
The option was awarded without competition because the government determined that only one responsible source could provide the required services.
Naval Sea Systems Command in Washington is the contracting activity for both awards.
The combined $20 million reflects the announced modification values, while only $1.5 million was expressly obligated at the time of the two announcements.

articles.title: Ramaphosa’s R100-million technology plan raises hopes for jobs
articles.snippet: Ramaphosa’s R100-million technology plan raises hopes for jobs Scrolla.Africa

News
Ramaphosa’s R100-million technology plan raises hopes for jobs
President Cyril Ramaphosa during his visit to Silicon Valley in the United States, where he announced plans for a R100-million technology fund. Picture: The Presidency
By
Palesa Matlala
23rd November 2026
Share
5 Min Read
LANGUAGE:

Listen to this article.
President Cyril Ramaphosa says entrepreneurs have proposed a R100-million fund to help South African businesses develop artificial intelligence and compete internationally.
With 8.6 million South Africans unemployed, experts say better training and work experience are needed to help young people find jobs.
Millions of South Africans are desperate for jobs, and President Cyril Ramaphosa believes new technology could help create opportunities for young people.
The president has announced plans for a R100-million fund to support South African businesses developing artificial intelligence.
The announcement follows his week-long visit to Silicon Valley in the United States, where he met technology companies and investors.
Artificial intelligence is technology that helps computers perform tasks such as answering questions, solving problems and working with information.
Ramaphosa said South African entrepreneurs who joined the trip proposed the fund.
“We walk away from Silicon Valley with commitments made by some of our own entrepreneurs that have come up with an idea that we should set up a venture capital fund that will start off with R100 million,” he said.
The money would help small technology businesses develop products, grow and possibly employ more people.
But South Africa faces a much bigger challenge.
According to Statistics South Africa, 8.6 million people were unemployed between July and September 2026. The unemployment rate stood at 33.7%.
For many young people, finding work remains difficult even after completing their studies.
A World Bank report published in August 2026 found that South Africa has unemployed graduates while some technology companies struggle to find workers with the right skills.
The report identified shortages in computer programming, networking and online security skills.
It also found that employers want people who can communicate well, solve problems and work with others.
The findings point to a possible solution: train unemployed young people in skills that businesses actually need.
Schools, colleges and universities could work more closely with employers to offer practical training and work experience.
Technology companies receiving government support could also be encouraged to hire and train young South Africans.
Another option is to make technology training available in townships and rural communities, where young people may struggle to afford computers, data and transport.
Community centres, libraries and schools could offer affordable Internet access and basic computer lessons.
Small businesses also need support.
Young people running businesses in townships could benefit from easier access to funding, business training and opportunities to sell their products and services.
But technology alone will not solve unemployment.
Economists at Nedbank, in their November 2026 labour market report, warned that businesses were not creating enough jobs to keep up with the growing number of people looking for work.
The report showed that South Africa gained 101,000 jobs in the third quarter, but the number of unemployed people still increased.
